# Setaketujātaka (Ja 377)

**ID:** Ja 377
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Setaketujātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Setaketujātaka* (Ja 377) is a birth story set in the Jetavana monastery, where the Buddha delivers the discourse concerning a deceitful monk (*kuhakabhikkhu*) [Fausböll 1883]. In the story of the past, King Brahmadatta rules in Benares while the Bodhisatta is a renowned teacher (*disāpāmokkhācariya*) of five hundred pupils [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. His senior student, a northern brahmin named Setaketu, is exceptionally arrogant about his caste [Law 1931; Cowell 1897]. When Setaketu insults a *caṇḍāla* to avoid being touched by wind carrying his scent, the *caṇḍāla* poses a riddle regarding the "quarters" (*disā*) and humiliates him by pinning him between his feet [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. The teacher comforts and admonishes the indignant youth with the opening verse beginning *Mā tāta kujjhi na hi sādhu kodho* ("Friend, be not angry") [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. Setaketu later completes his education at Takkasīlā and wanders the country learning practical arts before assuming the leadership of five hundred ascetics [Law 1931; Cowell 1897]. Arriving in Benares, he stages hypocritical ascetic feats—including thorn-beds and the five-fire penance—to secure royal favor until his fraudulent conduct is broken by the king's royal priest (*purohita*) [Fausböll 1883; Cowell 1897]. In the identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that Setaketu was the deceitful monk, the *caṇḍāla* was Sāriputta, and the royal priest was the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1883].

 DharmaNexus confirms this close connection, finding that verses §3.1–6.4 of Ja 377 share a substantial passage (similarity 0.95) with Ja 487 (§0.4–4.4), while also exhibiting extensive text reuse across the commentary traditions in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].

- Passage-level parallels: Ja 487 Uddālakajātaka
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§1.1–2.4 ↔ §2077_9–2083); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Catuttho bhāgo) (Atk S0513a4) (§5.4–6.4 ↔ §2852–2853); Uddālakajātaka (Ja 487) (§3.1–6.4 ↔ §0.4–4.4)
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database — Pali-internal text reuse matches between Ja 377, Ja 487, and Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā.

- [Law 1931] Bimala Churn Law, ed., Buddhistic Studies (1931) — Details of Setaketu's education at Takkasīlā and leadership of five hundred ascetics.
- [Fausböll 1883] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 3 (1883) — Pali text, narrative framing, verse incipit, and birth identification.
